uncertain.mcp: Discord's developer docs (docs.discord.com/llms.txt) document no API MCP server; docs.discord.com/mcp is a docs-search-only MCP (Mintlify-style). However a live, Discord-hosted, OAuth-protected MCP endpoint exists at https://mcp.discord.com (protected-resource metadata names Discord as resource and discord.com as auth server; read-only 'personal.*' scopes). It is undocumented/unannounced and discord.com's OAuth metadata has no dynamic client registration endpoint, so it is likely limited to allow-listed clients. Labeled official_remote on the evidence of the vendor-hosted endpoint; if graders count only publicly documented, generally usable servers, the label would be community_only. Evidence for mcp.discord.com is from direct HTTP probes (headers/JSON), not a docs page.
uncertain.auth_primary: OAuth2 is offered, but user bearer tokens only cover identity-type scopes; most actions (messages, channels, moderation) require the bot token, and OAuth2 is mainly used to install the bot into a guild. Chose bot_token; a toolkit could arguably be described as oauth2 (install) + bot_token (calls).

notes: Discord docs moved from discord.com/developers/docs to docs.discord.com/developers (301). Privileged intents review threshold changed from 100 servers to 10,000 unique users. App creation and bot tokens are free; no paid tier for API. Also a docs-only MCP exists at docs.discord.com/mcp (tools: search_documentation_discord, query_docs_filesystem_documentation_discord).
